title: Attention Maps Know When to Think: Training-Free Difficulty-Aware Chain-of-Thought for Reasoning Segmentation
summary: Attention-map entropy was used as a training-free difficulty signal to choose whether a multimodal language model should use chain-of-thought reasoning for reasoning segmentation. The framework also used bidirectional rethinking when initial output failed; benchmark results and efficiency are limited to the reported tasks.
ai_technology: Attention-map entropy used as a difficulty signal for reasoning segmentation
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: DA-CoT used attention entropy to gate chain-of-thought and reported state-of-the-art performance on the reported reasoning-segmentation benchmarks with improved inference efficiency.
evidence.unknown: The benchmark result is limited to the evaluated models and tasks; it does not establish general reasoning gains across modalities or applications.
evidence.ai_role: Attention-map entropy from a multimodal language model signals task difficulty and determines whether to trigger chain-of-thought; bidirectional rethinking can reverse the decision after a failed output.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
